cap: Carcinoma in situ fills a duct or lobule but stays inside the basement membrane, with myoepithelial cells still around it; invasion begins when tumor cells cross that membrane and the stroma turns desmoplastic. DCIS calcifies through comedo necrosis, while lobular cells lose E-cadherin (the CDH1 product), fall apart and later invade in single file.
teach: Read each row left to right as time. Atypia comes before carcinoma in situ, and carcinoma in situ comes before invasion. The duct outline is the basement membrane: while it is intact and ringed by myoepithelial cells, the lesion cannot reach lymphatics, which is why DCIS and LCIS do not metastasize.
